Examples of how these questions

Giving Feedback or Noting Discrep-
ancy: Occasionally it is necessary to
confront a client who may be providing
information that is either inconsistent
or contradictory or excuses for not
making changes. This form of question-
ing is especially valuable if a client is
in denial or is expressing resistance
to change. Bauer and Sokolik note a
variety of ways that the counselor can
bring these discrepancies to the atten-
tion of the client.20
•
State observation without adding
“but”; use “and” as the connector.
Following the “and” is the observa-
tion of the discrepancy.
• Begin the statement with “on the
one hand . . . on the other hand . . .”
• Directly say “I see/ hear an
inconsistency . . .”
